styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: The Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen in one golden triangle.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Tapas crawls, market stalls and late dinners.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Royal palace, old streets and Habsburg Madrid.

stays.why: Dead centre, walk to the Prado, Plaza Mayor and Royal Palace. Metro hub under the square. Noisy at night.
Theatre strip with shops and big-name hotels. Walk to Sol and Chueca; lively late into the night.
Old-town lanes, Sunday El Rastro market and the best tapas bars. Quiet mornings, busy weekends.
Elegant, calm and upscale. Good for shopping and quiet nights; a longer walk or short metro ride to the old centre.

food: Do a tapas crawl: order one small plate and a drink per bar, then move on. Dinner starts late, often after 21:00.
Try local dishes: tortilla española, jamón ibérico, patatas bravas, cocido madrileño and bocadillo de calamares near Plaza Mayor.
Markets are good value: Mercado de San Miguel for snacks, San Antón and San Fernando for cheaper local stalls.
Book popular restaurants ahead, especially on weekends. Many close one day midweek; check before you go.
Late-night eats: churros con chocolate after midnight, and bars around Sol and La Latina stay open very late.
more_time: Day trip to Toledo: train from Atocha in about 35 minutes; a walled old city full of history.
Day trip to Segovia: high-speed train in under 30 minutes for the Roman aqueduct and the Alcázar.
Art lovers: swap a city day for the Reina Sofía's Guernica and the Thyssen collection, or add El Escorial by train.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Prado and Reina Sofía, the old centre and a proper tapas crawl without rushing.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 10°C and lows around 1°C. Pack a warm coat; few rainy days.
February: still cool, highs near 13°C. Quiet season, good for museums.
March: mild at 16°C but one of the wetter months, about 9 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
April: pleasant highs near 19°C, lows around 7°C. Also wet, around 9 rain days.
May: warm and mostly dry, highs near 24°C. One of the best months to visit.
June: hot and dry, highs near 30°C. Sightsee early and late; midday is harsh.
July: very hot, highs near 34°C, almost no rain. Plan indoor afternoons.
August: hot, highs near 33°C. Many local shops and restaurants close for holidays; check opening times.
September: warm at 27°C and drier than spring. A strong month for sightseeing.
October: mild at 22°C but wet, around 9 rain days. Carry a light rain jacket.
November: cooler at 15°C with about 8 rain days. Fewer crowds at the museums.
December: cold, highs near 12°C and lows around 3°C. Festive lights; pack layers.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate: hot, dry summers and cool winters, with the wettest spells in spring and autumn.

items.title: Best months: May, June, September
items.text: Warm days around 24–30°C and mostly dry. Great for walking the old centre.

items.title: Summer is very hot (July–August)
items.text: Highs near 33–34°C with little rain. Do museums at midday and walk in the morning or evening.

items.title: Wettest in spring and autumn
items.text: March, April and October each see around 9 rain days. Pack a small umbrella.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: January highs near 10°C and lows around 1°C. A warm coat and layers are essential.

items.title: Sunny most of the year
items.text: Even wet months have plenty of bright days. Sunscreen matters from spring to autumn.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and a hat for summer; a warm coat for winter; a rain layer for March, April and October; comfortable shoes for cobbled streets.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; walk the old centre.

modes.text: 13 lines, fast and cheap. Single Zone A fare €1.50–2, airport supplement €3. A Multi Card costs €2.50 and is reloadable; a ten-trip Metrobús ticket is about €12.20.
Buses share the same tickets. Night buses run when the metro closes around 01:30.
Taxis are plentiful and metered. Uber, Cabify and Bolt operate in Madrid.
Not needed in the city. Use the metro and trains for day trips.
Best way to see the centre. Bikes and e-scooters are widely rented.
Unlimited travel: 1 day €10, 2 days €17, 3 days €22.50, 5 days €32.50, 7 days €41. Worth it if you ride often.
